instrument: Formalized manual usability check for the designated product's interactive surface — the human-facing approval prompts of the guard's auth code. This file formalizes the manual check in the guard tree's CONTRIBUTING.md ('Manual check of the prompts') with recorded outcome fields, per SPEC_Benchmark section 3's product-level framing of the usability dimension: the dimension turns on the product being interactive, and these prompts are the product's interactive surface, evaluated as user tasks by a person present.

record_fields.exercised: boolean: true only when this prompt class was actually exercised in the recorded run; false otherwise. A descriptive string is not a value of this field (the description of what the check exercises lives in exercise_steps)
record_fields.exercise_steps: what the manual check exercises for this prompt class (the CONTRIBUTING.md steps)
record_fields.observed: string or null: what the operator observed; null until the class is exercised
record_fields.outcome: one of outcome_vocabulary: 'pass' when every exercised task completed as the check's steps state, 'fail' when any did not (the failing step named in observed), 'not-run' until the class is exercised

records.exercise_steps: CONTRIBUTING.md manual check step 12 (and the Hello branch of steps 1 and 5): an over-cap extendable run on an account with Windows Hello set up; the Hello request is shown, answered correctly, answered wrongly / cancelled, and left unanswered while the starter exits.
records.outcome_fields: observed = what the operator saw (prompt shown or not, text legible in full, error text after a wrong answer, prompt's fate after timeout or starter exit); outcome = pass when every exercised task completed as the check's steps state, fail when any did not, with the failing step named in observed

records.exercise_steps: CONTRIBUTING.md manual check steps 1-5, 7 and 10: the secure-desktop credential dialog on an account without Hello — right password (including the long-command-line and look-alike-name variants of step 1), wrong password three times, cancel, PIN tile where offered, and no-answer / starter-exits cases; the pass criterion the check itself states for the text is that the Command line field is fully visible in the dialog, with any clipping recorded.
records.outcome_fields: observed = what the operator saw (fields shown, any clipping and the last field visible, incorrect-password text on the second and third prompts, dialog's fate after timeout or starter exit, per-account-type result for local / Microsoft / domain accounts); outcome = pass when every exercised task completed as the check's steps state, fail when any did not, with the failing step named in observed

records.exercise_steps: CONTRIBUTING.md manual check step 6: the console prompt from a real terminal with --authenticate console — right password, Esc / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Z behaviour as the step records it, the stored-credential non-use check, the piped-stdin refusal, the command-history clearing check (F7 / doskey /history after a known test password), and the console-mode restoration checks after Ctrl+C, after timeout, and after the starter exits (the shell must echo typed characters afterwards).
records.outcome_fields: observed = what the operator saw (the form of the account name shown, whether a user name was asked, each control key's result, whether any password line remained in the console history, whether the shell echoed after each ending); outcome = pass when every exercised task completed as the check's steps state, fail when any did not, with the failing step named in observed

revival: Run the tree CONTRIBUTING.md 'Manual check of the prompts' steps on an interactive Windows desktop before any release that changes src/auth.rs or src/sys.rs, as part of the ready-to-fly Windows run, and for each prompt class below set exercised to the boolean true, and fill in observed/outcome, from that run.
tier_note: A manual check is a manual check. No campaign slot and no test in this suite measures this surface; the outcomes below are recorded by the operator who runs the check on an interactive Windows desktop (the ready-to-fly Windows run), and until that run every outcome stands at 'not-run' — recorded as such, never as a pass.
